issues.legal_issue: The eviction regime for rent arrears depends on whether a dispute over standard rent remains unresolved when the eviction claim is considered.
material_facts: The tenant had applied to have the standard rent fixed and paid the provisional standard rent set by the court.
After the court fixed the standard rent, both the tenant and the landlord challenged that determination in revision proceedings, so the dispute continued.
The tenant paid the arrears calculated at the standard rent ultimately fixed and the suit costs before the eviction suit was decided.
issues.conclusion: Because the dispute over standard rent continued, the case fell under section 12(3)(b), not section 12(3)(a). The tenant had complied with the requirements for protection under clause (b), so the High Court's eviction order was set aside and the Assistant Judge's decision restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3)(a) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 applies only when its conditions coexist, including that there is no dispute regarding the amount of standard rent. Section 12(3)(b) governs other cases, including cases in which a dispute about standard rent continues, and bars eviction when the tenant meets its payment and cost requirements. Vasumatiben Gaurishankar Bhatt v. Naviram Mancharam Vora was distinguished because the dispute here continued through revisions; Vora Abbasbhai Alimahomed v. Haji Gulamnabi Haji Safibhai was cited in connection with a separate contention that the Court found it unnecessary to decide.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_suit: A landlord brought a suit seeking eviction of a tenant for rent arrears under a rent-control regime.
predicates.standard_rent_dispute_continued: The tenant or landlord continued to challenge the determination of standard rent, leaving the amount in dispute.
predicates.tenant_met_payment_and_cost_requirements: The tenant paid or tendered the rent required by the court and paid the suit costs as directed.

issues.definition: When an eviction suit for rent arrears involves a continuing dispute over standard rent and the tenant meets the required payment and cost conditions, the tenant is protected from eviction.
